title: Trace cache replaces conventional L1 instruction cache
decision: Decided to store decoded micro-ops in a trace cache rather than decoded micro-ops in a conventional L1 instruction cache fed by x86 decode
alternatives_or_rejected: Conventional L1 instruction cache that holds raw x86 and decodes on fetch (decoded-uop L1 also implied as the conventional alternative)
rationale: Decoupling fetch bandwidth from x86 decoding bandwidth; avoiding the complexity and decode cost on the hot fetch path; storing already-decoded traces ready for delivery to the allocation/rename stage
outcome: The paper states the trace cache supplies the renamed micro-ops stream directly to the out-of-order core, with trace-pack and segment build-up mechanisms described as building traces from decoded paths
weakest_point: Direction of the decision (trace cache chosen over conventional L1 I$) is almost certainly correct; exact wording and any explicit 'rejected alternative' framing is uncertain since I am reconstructing from memory of this paper

title: Double-pumped ALUs for rapid execution engine
decision: Chose to clock the integer ALUs at twice the core clock (double-pumped) so each ALU can complete up to two integer ops per core clock, rather than running ALUs at the core clock rate
rationale: Stated reasoning in the paper: simple integer ALU operations (add, compare, logic, shift) have latency short enough that halving their pipeline stage enables 2x integer execution throughput at modest cost; supported by low-latency ALU design rather than port replication
outcome: Paper reports this allows low-latency integer operations and high issue bandwidth on simple ALU ops, enabling the rapid execution engine characteristic
weakest_point: I am uncertain whether the paper explicitly justifies double-pumping via ALU latency analysis in the way I've stated, vs. merely describing it; direction of decision (double-pumped, not single-pumped) is high confidence

title: Deep pipeline (20 stages) chosen over shorter pipeline
decision: Adopted a deep pipeline (~20 stages) to enable high clock frequency
rationale: Paper's stated philosophy: deeper pipeline allows higher frequency scaling by breaking work into shorter stages; traded pipeline depth against branch misprediction / recovery cost
outcome: Paper presents the long pipeline as a fundamental design point underlying the frequency-targeted design of NetBurst
weakest_point: I am uncertain of the paper's specific stage-count phrasing and whether alternatives were ever discussed; this is closest to general P4 knowledge dressed as paper content

title: Bypass between trace cache miss and decode (μops delivered by decode trace cache miss)
where_in_paper: Trace Cache section, microarchitecture diagram and surrounding text
decision: Decided that on a trace cache miss, decoded micro-ops are delivered directly from the decode pipeline to the allocation/rename stage, rather than always going through the trace cache
rationale: Avoids serializing execution on trace cache build-up; maintains forward progress on branch/path that is not yet traced
outcome: Paper describes a μop delivery path from decode in parallel with the trace cache delivery, with mux/selection between the two at allocation
weakest_point: Whether the paper describes this as a 'design decision weighed' vs. just a structural fact is uncertain; the structural fact of decode-path-bypass is likely correct
